l.i: Quum a nostra, inquiunt, abhorreas religione, & te Christianum di-
cas, quaenam est tua religio? quae fides? Ia, inquit, fassus sum me tantum-
modo Christum eumque crucifixum praedicare. mea fides est ea quam
Christi Ecclesia per vniuersum orbem dispersa, omni tempore con-
fessa est, atque instituit. Vos autem corrupistis & plane peruertistis
synceraм doctrinam qua nobis Iesus Christus crucifixus proponitur:
atque aliud vitae genus abominabile suscepistis, vestraque impietate
magnam mundi partem in extremas miserias coniecistis. Sed quo ple-
nior meae fidei constet ratio, Credo in Deum Patrem, qui omnia crea-
uit: Credo in Deum Filium Iesum Christum, qui suo sanguine genus
humanum redemit, dum illud e faucibus inferorum & diaboli tyran-
nide eripiens, in Euangelij libertatem vindicauit: Credo in Deum Spi-
ritum sanctum, qui occulta quadam & diuina virtute credentes san-
ctificat. Credo propter Filium me gratuito peccatorum omnium remis-
sione potitum: Credo me solius Christi mediatoris beneficio, nullo meo
merito, nullaque operum satisfactione, aut Papali indulgentia prae-

page.notes: The word "praefultum" (line 5 of the Creed passage) is uncertain: the long s and f look alike in the scan, so it may be "praefultum" or another form. "Fraciscus" and "Cuculla-ti" are read from the print but the long s is hard to confirm. The italic/roman boundaries are judged from the scan: the accused's speech and creed are italic; the narrative from "His dictis" is roman. "vniuersum" and "synceraм" (the last has a stray Cyrillic-like character; it should read "syncerám" with a plain Latin letter) are transcribed as printed. Ink underlining and handwritten marks in the margins were not transcribed.
